hard_failures.falsifier: Exhibit a reading of lines 49-53 under which the visibility clause is equivalent to visibility.definition's single-q tail predicate (e.g. show the whole-geodesic and tail readings coincide, or that D4 binds gamma to a tail), or revise quantifiers.formal to the declared predicate: 'forall future-inextendible causal geodesics gamma with finite affine length: not exists q in I+, exists t0 in [0,T): tail gamma([t0,T)) subset J^-(q) intersect M'. If the revision lands at a new hash this verdict is superseded; if only the wording moves without changing the clause, HF-088-F1-1 stands.
hard_failures.finding: quantifiers.formal (lines 49-53) ends 'forall future-inextendible causal geodesics gamma of (M,g) with finite affine length: not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M' - whole-geodesic containment, with no t0 and no tail. visibility.definition (line 220) declares the class predicate as the single-q TAIL predicate: 'there exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M', and states 'requiring the whole geodesic to lie in J^-(q) would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region'. visibility.negation_conclusion (line 222) repeats that the whole-geodesic/B-containment reading is NOT equivalent. Since whole containment implies tail containment, the formal clause's negation of whole-geodesic containment is strictly weaker than the declared predicate's negation of tail containment: a development whose geodesic has a visible tail but is not wholly contained satisfies quantifiers.formal while violating the class conclusion. The frozen formal sentence is therefore not the class it is bound to; this is the same failure family as the previously corrected 'i.e. inside B' equivalence error and was flagged as a quantifier contradiction in ASTRA_HANDOFF pass 03.

hard_failures.finding: The frozen file repeats the top-level mapping key 'revised_at' seven times (lines 8,10,12,14,16,20,23) plus 'revised_at_unused' twice (26,28); strict YAML 1.2 parsers reject the document while PyYAML silently last-wins, so the revision metadata is parser-dependent and the rev4-rev11 delta comments are attached to keys with no effect. The last-wins values are also forward-dated relative to the bytes: revised_at=2026-09-12T00:30:00+08:00 and f0_binding.checked_at=2026-09-12T00:30:00+08:00 against a file mtime of 2026-09-12T00:19:14+08:00, i.e. the declared revision instant postdates the file by 645 s (CF-14 family; the artifact cannot have been revised at 00:30 and last written at 00:19). This is not counted as a semantic hard failure but blocks 'machine-frozen' and makes binding-at-instant claims unreliable.

score_rationale: The artifact is structurally complete (37/37 acceptance axes present, all six ordered binders resolve, the frozen binding gate returns PASS, the class-separation detector is clean and its regression corpus passes 17/17 leaks + 10/10 controls) and the conclusion identity is correctly WCC with SCC strengthenings explicitly forbidden. It nevertheless cannot be accepted at this hash: the operative quantifier clause uses whole-geodesic single-q containment, a reading the same file explicitly rejects and which is strictly weaker than the declared tail predicate (HF-088-F1-1, critical); the conclusion's machine statement uses an undefined symbol AF_{I+} (HF-088-F1-2); revision provenance is parser-dependent and forward-dated relative to the bytes' own mtime (HF-088-F1-3); the class_contract_pointer resolves only in the non-canonical authoring supplement (HF-088-F1-4); and the three G-FORM schemas still do not share one frozen data class (HF-088-F1-5). One critical + four major hard failures, no semantic defect in the class content itself.
